species.real: A British brass band has a fixed line-up of about 25 players, uses cornets instead of trumpets, and has only one section that isn't brass: the percussion.
species.name: Tootlet

dex.text: Practises its scales in the back room of the club every Tuesday, whether anyone asked or not. Its valve-button nose goes parp when it sneezes.
dex.fact: On Whit Friday, brass bands march from village to village round Saddleworth and Tameside, playing at each contest to an adjudicator hidden out of sight, so they are judged on sound alone.

species.real: Bombardon is an old name for the bass tuba, and many brass band instruments descend from the saxhorns patented in the 1840s by Adolphe Sax, of saxophone fame.
species.name: Bombardon

dex.text: Its oompah carries three valleys on a still night. Its idea of a quiet number is still worth a letter to the council.
dex.fact: Brass bands grew up around the mills and collieries of northern England in the 19th century, often backed by the owners; Black Dyke, founded at John Foster's mill in Queensbury in 1855, still plays today.
